assets.purpose: Ballista tower, first of the five missing towers and the first real generation under the approved art plan. A tall timber siege A-frame carrying a wide horizontal crossbow beam, deliberately unroofed so the silhouette cannot be confused with the roofed arrow tower at thumbnail size. Candidate only: art/director and the human judge it before the rest of the batch is spent.

assets.prompt: a ballista tower: a tall timber siege platform, not a building. Four splayed wooden legs form a narrow, tall A-frame that stands almost the full height of the frame, cross-braced with two horizontal beams. On top sits a giant crossbow: one thick horizontal bow axle spanning wider than the frame, two short swept bow arms, a heavy iron-tipped bolt loaded on the rail pointing up and toward the viewer, and a cranked winch drum with a hand crank at the back. Low stone footing block at the base only, no walls. Isometric 3/4 view, warm dusk palette, light from the top-left, isolated on a transparent background, the whole machine inside the canvas with nothing clipped at any edge, base flat on the bottom row, filling the canvas from side to side at the bow. The silhouette must read as a crossbow engine and never as a house or a watchtower: no roof, no conical or gabled top, no crenellations, no pinnacle, no stone shaft. No grass, no ground tile, no plinth, no shadow ellipse. Same rendering and palette as art/style/anchor.png.

assets.prompt: a mortar tower: a squat, wide, heavy stone gun emplacement, not a building. A short thick drum of stacked rough stone blocks, wider than it is tall, sits on a broad flat footing slab with a chamfered rim resting on the bottom row. Through the drum rises a thick iron-banded mortar tube angled steeply upward and slightly toward the viewer, its wide empty bore opening facing up so a dark round hole reads at the very top of the silhouette; a low collar ring and two rivet bands wrap the barrel. Two sandbag-stone blocks and three round stone shells lie on the footing beside the tube. The top of the silhouette is the open mouth of the tube, never a roof: no roof, no gable, no cone, no crenellation, no pinnacle, no tall shaft. No splayed legs, no A-frame, no crossbow, no horizontal bow beam, no winch. Isometric 3/4 view, warm dusk palette, light from the top-left, isolated on a transparent background, the whole machine inside the canvas with nothing clipped at any edge, base flat on the bottom row, the footing filling the canvas almost side to side. Thumbnail silhouette: a wide squat mortar, unmistakably neither the tall roofed arrow tower nor the open-framed ballista. No grass, no ground tile, no plinth, no shadow ellipse. Same rendering and palette as art/style/anchor.png.

assets.prompt: a rime tower: a tall, narrow ice-and-frost siege tower, not a house. A single slender square shaft of pale frost-veined stone rises almost the full height of the frame, only about a third as wide as it is tall, its faces carved with sharp vertical flutes and a thin rim of rime at each course. The crown is a bristling cluster of four to six tall angular ice crystal shards of different heights, the tallest slightly off centre, each sharply pointed with a bright glint on its top-left facet; the crystal crown is the widest part of the tower and is spiky, never a roof. Two small ice shards float free above and beside the crown. A narrow band of blue-white frost wraps the shaft at mid height with one hanging icicle. Low stone footing block at the base only: one narrow block of grey stone under the shaft, no wider than the shaft, resting on the bottom row, nothing beside it and nothing around it. The tower fills the canvas from the bottom row upward, the tallest crystal reaching near the top of the frame with clear margin, nothing cut. The top of the silhouette is sharp crystal points: no pyramid, no gable, no cone roof, no flat roof slab, no crenellations, no dome. No timber beams, no crossbow, no barrel, no winch, no splayed legs, no drum, no cannon. Cold palette only: deep teal, slate, cool grey stone, violet shadow, pale white-blue glints on the ice; no copper, no orange, no gold, no brown, no foliage green. Isometric 3/4 view, cold light from the top-left, isolated on a transparent background, nothing clipped at any edge, base flat on the bottom row. Thumbnail: a tall slim tower crowned with sharp crystal spikes, unmistakably neither the wide squat mortar nor the roofed arrow tower nor the open-framed ballista. No grass, no ground tile, no plinth, no platform, no moss, no green of any kind, no shadow ellipse. Same rendering and outline as art/style/anchor.png.

assets.verdict: REJECTED at art/STYLE.md canvas fill: widest row 18 px against the 24 px floor for a tapering-top tower (and against 32 px for a flat-topped one). The content box is 24x63 only because the two floating shards sit at different rows on either side of the crown; no single row of the sprite is wider than 18 px, and the shaft is about 12 px. At 1x on the 960x576 board that is a stick next to the 28 px arrow tower, which is the readability failure the floor exists to prevent. It cannot be repaired by post: an outline pass adds no width, and horizontal scaling would be authoring, not post-processing.
assets.secondary_defect: The call requested style_options.outline true but the output contains no ink #1b1a26 at all: 0/171 silhouette boundary pixels are ink, and #1b1a26 is absent from the sprite's tone set. Every delivered tower so far arrived at 129/129, 169/172 and 293/293, i.e. nearly complete, so this is an outlier of the route rather than a routine post step - it would have meant authoring a 171-pixel outline over the whole silhouette, which is outside a 'complete the 1px outline' pass.
post_processing: none. No post pass was run and no tower-rime-candidate.png was produced: the barrier is the silhouette's width, which post-processing cannot change. Making a failing sprite look finished with an outline and a palette check is exactly what T-0094 refused to do, and the same reasoning applies here.

The problem is that it is too slim, and that the teal-and-white crown reads at 1x as a frosted tuft or a flame rather than as faceted ice; the crystal identity is carried by the glints on two shards, not by the mass of the crown.
assets.re_attempt_note: For the next funded call: keep the cold wording and the corrected footing wording, and state a width floor in pixels instead of a ratio - 'the shaft is at least 32 px wide, the same width as the arrow tower's body, so the tower fills one whole tile', 'the crystal crown spans nearly the full canvas width', and 'the outer edge of the silhouette is a continuous 1 px dark ink outline all the way round'. The ratio wording ('about a third as wide as it is tall') is what produced an 18 px tower: it describes proportions correctly and still lands under the locked floor, because the floor is absolute, not proportional.
